stages.text:
F-35A Lightning II — First Flight
kind: documentary
style: Live-action widescreen documentary realism; steady tracking views, natural daylight, and AA-1’s documented proportions, geometry and markings.
In the opening two seconds, a widescreen live-action view shows AA-1, the first F-35A Lightning II prototype, lifting off at Lockheed Martin in Fort Worth, Texas, at 12:44 p.m. Central Standard Time on December 15, 2006. The title reads “F-35A Lightning II.” Chief pilot Jon Beesley remains an indistinct silhouette beneath the dark canopy.

The gray aircraft rises nose-high above the pale runway, with its nose gear and both main landing-gear assemblies extended. Its pointed nose, slender test probe, swept wings, side intakes and two outward-canted tail fins match the documented aircraft. From seconds two through five, “One engine” appears; calm English narration says, “The F-35A has one engine.”

From seconds five through eight, the view follows AA-1 flying after departure. “Conventional takeoff” replaces the previous fact label, while the narrator says, “It takes off from a conventional runway.” These successive views show an excerpt of the inaugural development test flight, not its full thirty-five-minute duration.

For the eight-second film, show runway acceleration and liftoff, then an airborne view. Keep 'F-35A Lightning II' visible; introduce 'One engine' and 'Conventional takeoff' in turn. Suggested calm English narration: 'The F-35A Lightning II. One engine. Conventional takeoff from a runway.'

items.prompt: An 8-second widescreen mini-documentary introducing the real F-35A Lightning II. Live-action documentary realism, 16:9, natural daylight, one steady tracking shot. The gray prototype has a pointed angular nose, slender nose test probe, dark canopy, side intakes, swept wings, two outward-canted tail fins and one rear exhaust nozzle. Keep realistic proportions: length roughly 1.46 times wingspan. The pilot is an indistinct dark silhouette. 0–2 s: Track from a slightly rearward side angle as the aircraft accelerates along a broad pale runway beside dry yellow-brown grass, with distant leafless trees beneath pale blue sky. Its nose rises and its wheels leave the pavement by 2 s; light gear struts and dark tires remain extended. Show 'F-35A Lightning II' at lower left for these two seconds, medium-large white sans-serif lettering on a translucent charcoal backing. Hear a powerful single-engine roar and outdoor air noise. 2–4.5 s: Continue tracking the same aircraft flying just above the runway in a shallow climb, with believable lift and speed. Replace the label with 'One engine', same position and styling, held still for 2.5 seconds. Over the softened engine sound, a calm adult English narrator says exactly: 'The F-35A has one engine.' 4.5–8 s: The tracking view tilts gently upward as the aircraft gains height, still flying forward. Replace the label with 'Conventional takeoff', same styling, held still through the final frame. The narrator says exactly: 'It makes a conventional runway takeoff.' Finish in flight, not landing. No other text, no cuts, no music, no subtitles, no sci-fi geometry, no hovering or vertical takeoff.

Red Kidney Bean: Seed to Seedling
kind: explainer
style: Live-action macro realism with simple growth animation, a fixed widescreen camera, and overhead illumination.
In the opening two seconds, a fixed widescreen live-action close-up shows a dry red kidney bean planted in perlite, its hard coat and hilum visible. Simple animation compresses the documented growth sequence: the bean absorbs water, swells, and its coat progressively loosens rather than disappearing. The voice-over begins: “A seed takes in water.”

From seconds two to five, the radicle emerges and extends downward in response to gravity; lateral roots begin forming as the cotyledons swell. The first leaves remain within the loosening coat before beginning to appear alongside the cotyledons. The narration continues: “Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.”

In the final three seconds, the first leaves push upward past the cotyledons on an upright stem beneath overhead illumination. The two unifoliate leaves unfold and expand, revealing the terminal growing tip, with the developing root system visible below. The sequence ends on this young seedling, without on-screen text or music.
